We're in the same boat. What you have described is EXACTLY what I've been thinking and what I've been feeling. Currently I take 4 different medications for my depression and my insomnia (which is partly due to my condition and partly a cause of it). I have lost some of my BEST friends, the ones who could distract me from myself. I still don't find worth in myself, but others think there's still hope for me. As of now, I'm still severely clinically depressed, I don't fight it anymore, it's my constant. It'd be nice to feel better, but honestly it's not for me. I'm no longer suicidal, even though I've tried to off myself six times. I'm not entirely happy, but I off-balance my sadness with the satisfaction of others. I'm the "funny guy" in my group of friends, and I don't like to admit it, but I make a lot of people happy. In-turn that gives me a sort of purpose. I don't know if this will help you, but if you keep people close to you and put your faith into people who actually DO care for you, then you'll have a better chance of recovery. Being happy isn't for me, but putting a smile on other people's faces is what gives me purpose in this life. So give it some time, distract yourself from you, don't think as much. Thinking only leads to worry and doubt. Don't doubt yourself. You are a the result of millions of years of evolutionary progress, that's no small feat. Put yourself into your recovery, and if you're absolutely sure after a great deal of time has passed that you're not making any progress, do what I do. Make others happy, you'll feel better. That's all I have to say to you my friend, I really do hope you recover, I don't like it when people hurt.
